about: Calls, prizes, technical assistance, readiness windows and procurement notices: one record per round, never reopened by date. Closed rounds stay as the archive. Status is computed (heat-economy/funding-core.js), never typed, except the source's own word in stated_status. Schema and rules: README.md.

deadline_history.note: earlier deadline as given in listings elsewhere; the official page says the deadline was extended

records.title: Nexa Lighthouse: Transition to Scale funding for climate and health innovation in Asia and the Pacific

purpose.text: Funds proven innovations that help local health actors turn climate-risk signals into timely action, for hazards including extreme heat.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Extreme heat is one of the hazards named in the call.

eligibility.text: Applicants incorporated and implementing in countries across Asia and the Pacific; the full list of eligible countries is in Appendix B of the funding opportunity.
eligibility.lead_text: Incorporated in an eligible country in Asia or the Pacific.

geography.text: Projects implemented in eligible countries in Asia and the Pacific, listed in Appendix B of the funding opportunity.

amount.text: USD 250,000 to 2,000,000 per innovation, at the partners' discretion depending on maturity

records.title: IKI Medium Grants 2026

purpose.text: Climate action and biodiversity projects in ODA-eligible countries, led by organisations based in Germany with local partners.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Adaptation has been a theme in past rounds; a heat project's fit depends on the 2026 funding announcement's priorities.

eligibility.text: Organisations established in Germany, with one or two local implementing partners in the implementation country.

geography.text: One or two ODA-eligible countries in the Global South.

records.conflict: The IKI page lists Medium Grants 2026 as closed; secondary listings gave a deadline of 12 January 2027. The official page is followed here.

records.title: IKI Small Grants: eighth call

purpose.text: Local climate and biodiversity projects by non-profit organisations in ODA-eligible countries.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: A local adaptation project could address heat; fit with the call's themes needs confirming.

eligibility.text: Sub-national, national and regional non-profit organisations in ODA-eligible countries.

core: Apply for the 8th International Call for Proposals
records.note: The registration deadline was not found on the official pages at the check; secondary listings give 8 January 2027. Check the call page.

records.title: APN calls for proposals 2026: CRRP and CAPaBLE

purpose.text: Regional research and scientific capacity development on global change in Asia and the Pacific.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Heat and health research in Asia can fit global change themes; heat is not named as a priority.

eligibility.text: Researchers and institutions in APN member countries, usually in multi-country teams.

geography.text: Asia and the Pacific (APN member countries).

records.title: GCF Readiness support: proposals accepted at any time, recommended by 31 March 2027

purpose.text: Readiness support for national institutions, country programming and direct access entities; submissions may be made at any time during the Readiness Strategy 2024 to 2027.
purpose.term: Submissions may be made at any time

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Readiness can support adaptation planning that covers heat, where national priorities include it.

eligibility.text: National Designated Authorities, or entities they nominate; not open to other organisations directly.

geography.text: Developing countries that are Parties to the UNFCCC.

deadlines.wording: recommended proposal submission date of no later than 31 March 2027

core: Submissions may be made at any time

records.title: Horizon Europe: integrating climate-related exposures into the human exposome (HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-ENVHLTH-02)

purpose.text: Research on climate-related exposures and how the human exposome changes with climate change.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Heat is a climate-related exposure; the topic is about the exposome broadly.

eligibility.text: Consortia; international cooperation is encouraged. Whether a partner from a given Asian country receives EU funding depends on Horizon Europe's country list.

geography.text: Not limited to Europe for participation; funding of non-European partners depends on the country list.

records.conflict: Published deadlines for this topic differ between sources (17 February 2027 and 13 April 2027); check the Funding and Tenders portal.

records.title: CTCN and Adaptation Fund: Climate Adaptation Innovation in Asia Pacific

purpose.text: Technical assistance for climate adaptation innovations in Asia and the Pacific.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Adaptation innovations for heat fall within the call's scope; it was not heat-specific.

eligibility.text: Applicants in the Asia Pacific region, as the call defined.

records.title: UNICEF Venture Fund: funding frontier climate tech for children's health

purpose.text: Equity-free funding for early-stage climate and health technology for children.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: The call cited children's exposure to extreme heat.

eligibility.text: Early-stage technology companies, as the call defined.

geography.text: Programme countries, as the call defined.

records.title: Commonwealth Foundation open grants call 2026 to 2027

purpose.text: Grants to civil society organisations and collectives; climate and environmental justice is one of three priorities.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Civil society work on heat could fit the climate and environmental justice priority.

eligibility.text: Not-for-profit organisations and collectives registered in eligible Commonwealth member countries.

geography.text: Eligible Commonwealth member countries (see the Foundation's eligible countries list); a project is implemented at least in the applicant's country of registration.

records.title: Global EbA Fund: small-size grants, eighth call

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Ecosystem-based measures such as urban greening can lower heat; fit depends on the call's priorities.

eligibility.text: Organisations as the call defined, with a focus on the least developed countries and small island states.

geography.text: ODA-eligible countries, with priority for least developed countries and small island states.

purpose.text: Resilience innovations across the Global South.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Themes are set each year; heat was not confirmed as a 2026 theme.

records.title: UNDP India RFP-050-IND-2026: workplan for a 'heat-smart' city and a digital heat-resilience toolkit

purpose.text: A firm to develop a workplan for a heat-smart city and an interactive digital heat-resilience toolkit.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Heat resilience in a city is the subject of the procurement.

eligibility.text: Firms responding to the request for proposals (a procurement, not a grant).

records.title: ILO request for quotation: desk review and evidence mapping of occupational exposure to excessive heat in Thailand

purpose.text: Desk review and evidence mapping of occupational exposure to excessive heat and its impacts on workers' safety and health in Thailand.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Occupational heat exposure is the subject.

eligibility.text: Suppliers responding through the UN Global Marketplace.
